name: Mhondoro
body:
MHONDORO
CR 4

This lion lacks a mane, but looks no less regal for it, regarding you with a soulful gaze.

XP 1,200
LN Large magical beast
Init +7; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, scent; Perception +9

DEFENSE

AC 15, touch 12, flat-footed 12 (+3 Dex, +3 natural, –1 size)
hp 37 (5d10+10); regeneration 5 (electricity, force, or sonic)
Fort +8, Ref +9, Will +6; Resist negative energy 10

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft.
Melee bite +8 (1d8+4 plus grab), 2 claws +8 (1d6+4)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 5 ft.
Special Attacks pounce, rake (2 claws +8, 1d4+4), terrifying roar

STATISTICS

Str 19, Dex 17, Con 15, Int 14, Wis 16, Cha 12
Base Atk +5; CMB +10 (+14 grapple); CMD 23 (27 vs. trip)
Feats Cosmopolitan, Improved Initiative, Run, Skills Acrobatics +11 (+15 when jumping), Knowledge (history)* +10, Knowledge (nobility)* +10, Perception +9, Stealth +8 (+12 in undergrowth); Racial Modifiers +4 Acrobatics when jumping, +4 Stealth (+8 in undergrowth)
Languages Common, plus any two
SQ ancestral vigor, possess host

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Ancestral Vigor (Su)

A mhondoro gains a +2 insight bonus to its saving throws (already included in the statistics above).

Cosmopolitan (Ex)

A mhondoro retains worldly knowledge and memories from its previous life. It selects two Intelligence-, Wisdom-, or Charisma-based skills and treats these as class skills. It also knows two additional languages. *The mhondoro listed above has Knowledge (history) and Knowledge (nobility) as class skills, but other mhondoro can have different skills.

Possess Host (Su)

As a standard action, a mhondoro can possess an adjacent willing humanoid, who gains the mhondoro-possessed template.

When it does this, the mhondoro’s lion form ceases to exist. If the host is reduced to negative hit points or dies while being possessed by the mhondoro, the mhondoro is expelled and its lion form reappears in the closest empty square.

While possessing a host, a mhondoro remains aware of the host’s actions and maintains an empathic link, akin to that between a spellcaster and a familiar. This allows the mhondoro to express its approval or disappointment of the host’s actions. If displeased with its host, the mhondoro can attempt to magically influence the host to comply. The host must succeed at a DC 15 Will save, or fall under the effect of a charm person with regard to the mhondoro for the next 12 hours. The host doesn’t gain the benefit of the ancestral vigor ability on saving throws to resist this charm ability.

A host who succeeds on the saving throw doesn’t realize that the mhondoro attempted to affect its mind. If the host takes hit point damage while under the charm person effect, it immediately attempts another saving throw to end this charm effect. The mhondoro can use this charm ability once per day, with this use refreshing at dawn. This ability is mind-affecting charm effect.

The save DC is Wisdom-based.

The mhondoro can end its possession at will, but the host cannot force a possessing mhondoro to leave. This possession is otherwise the equivalent of a ghost’s malevolence ability for purposes of effects that can suppress, expel, or otherwise affect possession.

Terrifying Roar (Su)

The mhondoro’s roar can cause even the stoutest of hearts to quail. As a standard action or in place of a bite attack, the mhondoro roars at a creature within 30 feet, who must succeed on a DC 15 Will save or become frightened for 1d4 rounds. Whether or not the save is successful, this creature is immune to the roar of that mhondoro for the next 24 hours. This is a mind-affecting fear affect. The save DC is Wisdom-based.

ECOLOGY

Environment warm plains
Organization solitary
Treasure none

Lingering spirits of past kings, chiefs, and other great figures, mhondoro (also svikiro) inhabit maneless lions and lie in wait until they sense a host in need of their aid. When they sense such a creature, the mhondoro asks if that creature is willing to accept its aid, though it does not specify what form this aid will take. If the creature agrees, the mhondoro possesses it and aids the creature in its quest. How long a mhondoro inhabits its host varies based on the length and urgency of the host’s task. While most mhondoro are benevolent and attempt to honor the need of the creature they assist, some attempt to assert their will over the host. Even the most benevolent mhondoro exerts considerable influence over how the creature performs its quest—the “price” for its assistance.
